title: p says /p/
parentNote: Today is /p/, a pop rather than a sound you can hold: lips shut, then a puff of air. Hold a hand in front of your mouth and say it — the little breath they can feel on their palm is the whole sound, and it is why /p/ turns into "puh" so easily. "Puh-i-guh" will never come out as "pig", so keep it as short as a tap. If they mix it up with /m/, point out that both begin with the lips shut; the difference is that /m/ hums out of the nose and /p/ bursts out of the mouth.

activities.mouthCue: Shut your lips, hold the air in, then pop them open. Put your hand in front of your mouth and feel the puff.
activities.prompt: This one is over almost before it starts. Listen hard.
